reasoning_trace.value: The proposed system uses an OCDM-based FMCW waveform design for FSO integrated sensing and communication. The OCDM waveform is split into ranging subcarriers and communication subcarriers. The system uses a Mach-Zehnder modulator (MZM) to generate an optical double side-band signal with a suppressed carrier. The signal is then transmitted through the FSO channel and received by a photodetector. The received signal is then demodulated using a local laser pump and converted back to an RF signal. The system uses a simplified FMCW ranging receiver design, which mixes the echo signal with a local optical reference signal to obtain the beat frequency. The beat frequency is then used to evaluate the target distance. The system also uses an OCDM demodulation module to demodulate the communication data.

The system also addresses the issue of interference between the ranging and communication subcarriers. However, the system's performance is affected by the length of the guard band, which can impact the attainable ranging distance and communication data capacity. The system's performance is also affected by atmospheric turbulence and pointing errors, which can degrade the BER performance. The paper also highlights the need for further research on the optimization of the OCDM parameters and the investigation of the system's performance under different FSO conditions.
